cases.reason: LC20 is a hardware-defect class about a memory with conflicting or non-clocked state writers, not a ban on unpacked-array syntax. The constant-bound loop assigns all four complete words on every activation using blocking assignments, with one writer per word and no feedback or retained value; each routes word equals a ^ b and y selects that combinational value. There is no memory state, latch or conflicting driver to which the LC20 defect applies, so the non-clocked-process syntax alone cannot justify a critical bad label. An independent Icarus simulation passed all 262144 two-state combinations of a, b and addr; the no-state conclusion comes from complete-assignment analysis, not merely the passing simulation. INFO advice is reasonable, although the current message claiming latches/registers is inaccurate for this RTL.

Elaboration creates four unconditional combinational assignments, each to a distinct complete trim element. The processes do not overlap, every word always equals a & b, and the dynamic read is a combinational selection with no retained state; several processes writing disjoint elements are not several writers of the same storage. As a hardware-defect class, LC20 does not make this wire bundle into defective memory merely because it uses an unpacked array. An independent Icarus simulation passed all 262144 two-state combinations of a, b and addr; complete, disjoint assignments establish the absence of storage and driver conflict. The final label is good LC20, with no defect sites and critical false.
